answer: New identities enter through a single narrow inlet: each locks a 60,000 POA bond in a pigment vault where every proof of work is dyed with a unique pigment that cannot be copied or transferred. A pigment seen twice is flagged at once, and its owner must show fresh work from a real counterparty within one epoch. Fake pigment burns the bond, half to the reporter, the identity banned 14 epochs and its vault sealed. Forging 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 x 60,000 = 60,000,000 POA, while an honest agent pays one 60,000 POA bond once. The limit: pigments fade when honest work spans many unrelated domains.
